subtitle: Lesson 18 · Asynchronous JavaScript

caption: A rejected promise behind an await is thrown as a normal, catchable exception.
No try/catch means the rejection has nowhere to go — it surfaces as an unhandled rejection.

eyebrow: Catching it at the call site instead
caption: An async function still returns a promise, so .catch() on the call works just as well as try/catch inside it.

eyebrow: One catch for several awaited steps
caption: One try/catch block covers every awaited step inside it — any rejection anywhere jumps straight to catch.

steps.label: NEVER SWALLOW SILENTLY
steps.sub: An empty catch block hides real bugs
